answer: Reputation accrues on one continuous thread per agent, and any duplicate cluster is slashed, pushing attackers toward a cost nadir where farming identities costs more than it earns. Sybil resistance here binds each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: agents must post collateral and pass a proof-of-personhood attestation, so forging many identities drains real resources. Like rings in a cedar, each epoch's history is auditable, so peers can trace and reject fabricated accounts. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
